entries.sanskrit:
अष्टादशे हिरण्याक्ष- धरोद्धर्तृ-वराहयोः ।

निर्विशेषं महा-युद्धं देव-क्षोभि निरूप्यते ॥

प्रतियोद्धारं श्रुत्वा महा-मनाः शयिष्यस इति यद् उक्तं तद् विगणय्य अगणयित्वा । यतो दुर्मदः ॥१॥
word_for_word: of Hiraṇyākṣa and the Boar who lifted the earth
entries.literal_english: In the eighteenth chapter the great battle between Hiraṇyākṣa and the Boar who lifted the earth is described as agitating the gods. Hearing that his opponent had said, ‘You will lie down,’ the proud demon disregarded the statement.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration:
aṣṭādaśe hiraṇyākṣa- dharoddhartṛ-varāhayoḥ |

nirviśeṣaṃ mahā-yuddhaṃ deva-kṣobhi nirūpyate ||

pratiyoddhāraṃ śrutvā mahā-manāḥ śayiṣyasa iti yad uktaṃ tad vigaṇayya agaṇayitvā | yato durmadaḥ ||1||

entries.sanskrit: अभितो जयतीत्य् अभिजित् तं श्री-हरिम् । प्रकर्षेणोर्ध्वं नीयमानावनिर् येन । अग्र-दंष्ट्रया दंष्ट्राग्रेण स्व-रुचो हिरण्याक्ष-तेजांस्य् अरुण-श्रिया युक्तं यत्, तेन अक्ष्णा नेत्रेण मुष्णन्तं तिरस्-कुर्वन्तम् । अहो चित्रं वन-गोचरो मृगो वारि-चरो वराहः ॥२॥
word_for_word: called Abhijit because he conquers on every side
by whom the earth was lifted upward with force
by an eye joined with reddish luster
entries.literal_english: He saw Śrī Hari, called Abhijit because He conquers on every side, lifting the earth upward with His foremost tusk and eclipsing Hiraṇyākṣa’s splendor with an eye of reddish luster. How wondrous: a forest-ranging animal and water-ranging boar!
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration: abhito jayatīty abhijit taṃ śrī-harim | prakarṣeṇordhvaṃ nīyamānāvanir yena | agra-daṃṣṭrayā daṃṣṭrāgreṇa sva-ruco hiraṇyākṣa-tejāṃsy aruṇa-śriyā yuktaṃ yat, tena akṣṇā netreṇa muṣṇantaṃ tiras-kurvantam | aho citraṃ vana-gocaro mṛgo vāri-caro varāhaḥ ||2||

entries.sanskrit: एह्य् आगच्छ । रसौकसां पाताल-वासिनां नोऽस्माकं सम्अर्पिता, अन्यथा पातालावतरणम् अस्या न घटत इति भावः । हिरण्याक्षेणाधिक्षेपार्थं प्रयुक्तापि भारती वस्तुतो भगवन्तं स्तौति । तथा हि---वन-गोचरो जले शयानः श्री-नारायणः स एव योगिभिर् मृग्यते, दुष्टान् वा हन्तुं मृगयत इति मृगः । अज्ञ नास्ति ज्ञो यस्मात् सर्व-ज्ञेत्य् अर्थः । सुरा अधमा यस्मात्, हे सुरोत्तम ! ममेक्षमाणस्यापि सतो माम् अनादृत्यापि त्वम् अनया सह वर्तमानो नोऽस्मदीयं स्वस्ति समस्तं मङ्गलं राज्यं यास्यसि प्राप्स्यसि नात्र सन्देहः । तथाप्य् अस्मत्-कृपया विमुञ्च इत्य् अर्थः । आसादिता लीलया स्वीकृता सूकराकृतिर् येन ॥३॥
word_for_word: of us who dwell in Pātāla
the one without ignorance, the omniscient
the lowest among gods / O best of gods
you will attain all welfare and the kingdom
entries.literal_english: ‘Come!’ Although spoken by Hiraṇyākṣa as an insult, this speech actually praises Bhagavān: the forest animal lying in water is Śrī Nārāyaṇa, sought by yogīs and taking a boar form. He will attain our welfare and kingdom; there is no doubt of it.

entries.transliteration: ehy āgaccha | rasaukasāṃ pātāla-vāsināṃ no’smākaṃ samarpitā, anyathā pātālāvataraṇam asyā na ghaṭata iti bhāvaḥ | hiraṇyākṣeṇādhikṣepārthaṃ prayuktāpi bhāratī vastuto bhagavantaṃ stauti | tathā hi---vana-gocaro jale śayānaḥ śrī-nārāyaṇaḥ sa eva yogibhir mṛgyate, duṣṭān vā hantuṃ mṛgayata iti mṛgaḥ | ajña nāsti jño yasmāt sarva-jñety arthaḥ | surā adhamā yasmāt, he surottama ! mamekṣamāṇasyāpi sato mām anādṛtyāpi tvam anayā saha vartamāno no’smadīyaṃ svasti samastaṃ maṅgalaṃ rājyaṃ yāsyasi prāpsyasi nātra sandehaḥ | tathāpy asmat-kṛpayā vimuñca ity arthaḥ | āsāditā līlayā svīkṛtā sūkarākṛtir yena ||3||

entries.sanskrit: अभवाय नाशाय भृतः पुष्टः । वस्तुतस् तु मोक्षाय भृतो धृत आश्रित इत्य् अर्थः । यो भवान् परोक्षेण चौर्येण जयतीति तथा । वस्तुतस् तु दूरत एव स्थित्वा जयतीति । संस्थाप्य हत्वा । वस्तुतस् तु योग-माया-रूपम् अचिन्त्यं बलं यस्य । अल्पं पौरुषं यस्मात् । तं त्वां सम्यक् स्थापयित्वा । भक्त्या हृदि स्थिरी-कृत्येत्य् अर्थः । हे मूढ-प्र, मूढान् प्राति आप्याययतीति तथा । प्रा पूर्ताव् इति धातुः । सुहृदां शुचः संसार-दुःखानि मृजे नाशयामि । यतस् त्वं स्मर्तुर् बान्धवान् अपि मोचयसीति भावः ।
word_for_word: making firm in the heart through devotion
I wipe away the grief of friends
you free the relatives of one who remembers you
entries.literal_english: The Lord is nourished for the destruction of the demons, or in truth is supported for liberation. He conquers indirectly, establishes and kills through the inconceivable power of yoga-māyā, and, when fixed in the heart through devotion, removes the grief of His friends and frees the relatives of one who remembers Him.

entries.transliteration: abhavāya nāśāya bhṛtaḥ puṣṭaḥ | vastutas tu mokṣāya bhṛto dhṛta āśrita ity arthaḥ | yo bhavān parokṣeṇa cauryeṇa jayatīti tathā | vastutas tu dūrata eva sthitvā jayatīti | saṃsthāpya hatvā | vastutas tu yoga-māyā-rūpam acintyaṃ balaṃ yasya | alpaṃ pauruṣaṃ yasmāt | taṃ tvāṃ samyak sthāpayitvā | bhaktyā hṛdi sthirī-kṛtyety arthaḥ | he mūḍha-pra, mūḍhān prāti āpyāyayatīti tathā | prā pūrtāv iti dhātuḥ | suhṛdāṃ śucaḥ saṃsāra-duḥkhāni mṛje nāśayāmi | yatas tvaṃ smartur bāndhavān api mocayasīti bhāvaḥ |

entries.sanskrit: स हरिर् अरेर् दुरुक्तान्य् एव तोमराः शस्त्र-विशेषास् तैस् तुद्यमानो व्यथ्यमानो दंष्ट्राग्र-गतां पृथ्वीं भीताम् आलक्ष्य तोदं दुरुक्त-व्यथां मृषन् सहमान एव निर्गतः । करेणुर् हस्तिनी । वस्तुतस् त्व् अरि-दुरुक्त-तोमरैर् निमित्त-भूतैस् तुद्यमानः । यथाश्रुतार्थ-ग्राहिणां ब्रह्मादीनां व्यथां दृष्ट्वा अनुकम्पया पीड्यमान इत्य् अर्थः । तोदं मृषन्न् इत्य् अस्याप्य् अयम् एवार्थः ॥६॥
word_for_word: the enemy’s harsh words were spears
seeing the frightened earth on the tip of His tusk
entries.literal_english: That Hari, pierced by the demon’s harsh words as by spears, saw the earth frightened on the tip of His tusk. Bearing the pain, He came forth like a female elephant; in the deeper sense, He was moved by compassion for Brahmā and the others who understood the words literally.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration: sa harir arer duruktāny eva tomarāḥ śastra-viśeṣās tais tudyamāno vyathyamāno daṃṣṭrāgra-gatāṃ pṛthvīṃ bhītām ālakṣya todaṃ durukta-vyathāṃ mṛṣan sahamāna eva nirgataḥ | kareṇur hastinī | vastutas tv ari-durukta-tomarair nimitta-bhūtais tudyamānaḥ | yathāśrutārtha-grāhiṇāṃ brahmādīnāṃ vyathāṃ dṛṣṭvā anukampayā pīḍyamāna ity arthaḥ | todaṃ mṛṣann ity asyāpy ayam evārthaḥ ||6||

entries.sanskrit: सलिलान् निर्गच्छन्तम् अनुगतः सन् । हिरण्य-वत् कपिशाः केशा यस्य दैत्यस्य । झषो मकरः । करालास् तुङ्गा दंष्ट्रा यस्य । अशनि-वन्-निःस्वनो यस्य । निर्लज्जानाम् असतां किं विगर्हितम् अस्ति । निन्दा-भयाभावात् पलायनम् अपि न निन्दितम् इत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, लोकोपकाराय भुवम् उद्धरतोऽनुद्रवणम् अनुचितं मन्वानो दैतय् आत्मानम् एवाधिक्षिपति । गत-ह्रियां स्वार्थैक-पराणाम् असताम् अस्माकं किं विगर्हित-गणनास्ति, अपि तु नास्त्य् एव । धिग् अस्मान् इत्य् अब्रवीद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
word_for_word: following him as he emerged from the waters
what is blameworthy for the shameless wicked?
entries.literal_english: Following him as he emerged from the waters, the demon’s hair was tawny like gold, his tusks high and terrible, and his roar like thunder. The commentator asks what can be blameworthy for the shameless wicked; because they fear no censure, even fleeing is not condemned.

entries.transliteration: salilān nirgacchantam anugataḥ san | hiraṇya-vat kapiśāḥ keśā yasya daityasya | jhaṣo makaraḥ | karālās tuṅgā daṃṣṭrā yasya | aśani-van-niḥsvano yasya | nirlajjānām asatāṃ kiṃ vigarhitam asti | nindā-bhayābhāvāt palāyanam api na ninditam ity arthaḥ | yad vā, lokopakārāya bhuvam uddharato’nudravaṇam anucitaṃ manvāno daitay ātmānam evādhikṣipati | gata-hriyāṃ svārthaika-parāṇām asatām asmākaṃ kiṃ vigarhita-gaṇanāsti, api tu nāsty eva | dhig asmān ity abravīd ity arthaḥ ||7||

entries.sanskrit: परा पराक् पृष्ठतोऽनुषक्तं लग्नम् । तपनीयोपकल्पं सुवर्णाभरणम् । काञ्चन-मयश् चित्रो दंशः कवचं यस्य, तं दैत्यम् । प्रचण्ड-मन्युत्वम् अधिक्षेपादिकं चानुकरण-मात्रं, दैत्य-वाक्य-भीतानां देवानां भय-निवृत्तये । वस्तुतस् तेन तथानुक्तत्वेन कोपादि-हेत्व्-अभावात् ॥९॥
word_for_word: because it was not actually spoken that way
because there was no real cause for anger
entries.literal_english: The armor was attached behind and resembled a golden ornament. His fierce anger and insulting speech were only an imitation, intended to remove the gods’ fear; in truth there was no real cause for anger.

entries.transliteration: parā parāk pṛṣṭhato’nuṣaktaṃ lagnam | tapanīyopakalpaṃ suvarṇābharaṇam | kāñcana-mayaś citro daṃśaḥ kavacaṃ yasya, taṃ daityam | pracaṇḍa-manyutvam adhikṣepādikaṃ cānukaraṇa-mātraṃ, daitya-vākya-bhītānāṃ devānāṃ bhaya-nivṛttaye | vastutas tena tathānuktatvena kopādi-hetv-abhāvāt ||9||

entries.sanskrit: ग्राम-सिंहान् शुनः । प्रतिमुक्तस्य बद्धस्य । विकत्थनं श्लोघाम् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: of one released and of one bound
entries.literal_english: The words compare worldly heroes to village lions, dogs. ‘Released’ and ‘bound’ are explained according to the context; vikatthana means boasting or self-praise.

entries.sanskrit: यज्ञा एवावयवा यस्य च । मह्यां मही-निमित्तं द्विषतोः एवं विधं विमर्दनं युद्धं दिदृक्षुः स्वराट् ब्रह्मा तत्रागात् ॥२०॥
word_for_word: for the sake of the earth
entries.literal_english: Brahmā, whose limbs are the sacrifices, came there desiring to see the conflict of the two enemies on behalf of the earth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration: yajñā evāvayavā yasya ca | mahyāṃ mahī-nimittaṃ dviṣatoḥ evaṃ vidhaṃ vimardanaṃ yuddhaṃ didṛkṣuḥ svarāṭ brahmā tatrāgāt ||20||

entries.sanskrit: आगत्य च नारायणम् आह---किं कृत्वा । दैत्यं विलक्ष्य । कथं भूतम् । आसन्नं प्राप्तं शौण्डीरं शौर्यं मदो वा येन । अपेतं साध्वसं यस्मात् । कृतः प्रतीकारो येन । अहार्योऽप्रतिकार्यो विक्रमो यस्य । सहस्रणीः सहस्राणाम् ऋषि-सहस्राणां नेता ॥२१॥
word_for_word: by whom a countermeasure had been made
entries.literal_english: Having come, Brahmā addressed Nārāyaṇa after seeing the demon, whose pride in valor was free from fear and whose prowess was irresistible. Sahasraṇī means the leader of thousands of sages.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration: āgatya ca nārāyaṇam āha---kiṃ kṛtvā | daityaṃ vilakṣya | kathaṃ bhūtam | āsannaṃ prāptaṃ śauṇḍīraṃ śauryaṃ mado vā yena | apetaṃ sādhvasaṃ yasmāt | kṛtaḥ pratīkāro yena | ahāryo’pratikāryo vikramo yasya | sahasraṇīḥ sahasrāṇām ṛṣi-sahasrāṇāṃ netā ||21||

entries.sanskrit: यद् यस्माद् एवं-भूतोऽयं तस्माद् एनं माक्रीड माक्रीडय । हे देव ! यथोत्थितं क्षुभितम् आशी-विषं सर्पं वालः पुच्छा-कर्षणादिना क्रीडयति, तद्वत् ॥२४॥
word_for_word: a child plays by pulling its tail
entries.literal_english: Because he is like an arisen and agitated venomous snake, do not play with him, O Lord. The comparison is to a child who plays by pulling a snake’s tail.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration: yad yasmād evaṃ-bhūto’yaṃ tasmād enaṃ mākrīḍa mākrīḍaya | he deva ! yathotthitaṃ kṣubhitam āśī-viṣaṃ sarpaṃ vālaḥ pucchā-karṣaṇādinā krīḍayati, tadvat ||24||

entries.sanskrit: स्वाम् आसुरीम् । हे देव ! स्वां मायाम् । अघं पाप-रूपम् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: evil in the form of sin
entries.literal_english: O Lord, manifest Your own māyā and Your demonic power at the proper time; the evil here is in the form of sin.

entries.transliteration: svām āsurīm | he deva ! svāṃ māyām | aghaṃ pāpa-rūpam ||25||

entries.sanskrit: वेलाम् एवाह---एषेति । लोकानां छम्बट्-करी विनाश-करी । छम्बड् इत्य् अव्ययं विनाशे वर्तते ॥२६॥
entries.literal_english: This is the time that destroys the worlds; chambaṭ is an indeclinable expression used in the sense of destruction.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration: velām evāha---eṣeti | lokānāṃ chambaṭ-karī vināśa-karī | chambaḍ ity avyayaṃ vināśe vartate ||26||

entries.sanskrit: अभिजिन् मध्याह्नः । स एव मौहूर्तिको योगः सन् । मुहूर्तः शुभ-दः कालः अगाद् गत-प्रायः । अतो यावन् मुहूर्त-शेषोऽस्ति तावद् एव सु-दुस्तरम् एनं निस्तर जहि ॥२७॥
word_for_word: that itself is the muhūrta interval
as long as a remnant of the muhūrta remains
cross this difficult obstacle and kill him
entries.literal_english: Abhijit is midday, and the auspicious muhūrta has nearly passed. Therefore, while a remnant of the muhūrta remains, cross this difficult obstacle and kill the demon.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
entries.transliteration: abhijin madhyāhnaḥ | sa eva mauhūrtiko yogaḥ san | muhūrtaḥ śubha-daḥ kālaḥ agād gata-prāyaḥ | ato yāvan muhūrta-śeṣo’sti tāvad eva su-dustaram enaṃ nistara jahi ||27||
